answer: Require each agent to post a bond that is forfeited if its actions are later proven fraudulent, while capping how much influence newly created identities can earn until they build a history of verified work. A sybil attacker must fund every identity separately and keep those bonds locked up; exposing even one coordinated fake risks losing its stake. The oasis may sound like a fable, but yarrow-branded credentials alone prove nothing: the costly bond and earned reputation are what make mass impersonation expensive.
